# 11 Simple Graphs · Problems（简单图·章末习题）

本块覆盖书页 453–472，内容**全部**是第 11 章 *Simple Graphs*（简单图）的章末习题：从 Problem 11.39 的后半段接起（p453 开篇即该题的题干预备段与 (a)(b)(c) 三小问），依次经过 §11.7/§11.8/§11.9/§11.10 各节的 Practice / Homework / Class / Exam Problems，止于 Problem 11.70（p471）；p472 是章末 verso（左页）空白页，只有 running head（书眉）。本块没有正文小节标题，也没有 `## 11.x` 一级正文，只有三处题组标题（`Problems for Section 11.8` / `11.9` / `11.10`）。

体例上，习题题干保留英文原文（含原书编号、`true / false`、`Circle` 这类操作动词），每道题后一行〔习题原文，未译〕；不译的理由是习题是做题用的工作材料，改写措辞会悄悄改变题意。中文出现在三处：本导语、Figure 图注、`[译注]`。公式一律用 LaTeX 重排——原 PDF 的 text layer 会把 $\{T,F\}$ 输出成 `fT; F g`、把 $\to$ 输出成 `!`、把 $\le$ 输出成不可见字符，本块所有公式均已对照页面图像逐一还原。

（承上一块）Problem 11.39 在 p452 已给出 3-color-$f$-gate（3-着色的 $f$-gate）的背景；本页先把它定义完，再给出 NOT-gate 的例子与三个小问。

> Suppose $f$ is an $n$-argument truth function. That is,
```math
f : \{T, F\}^n \to \{T, F\}.
```
> A graph $G$ is called a 3-color-$f$-gate iff $G$ has $n$ designated input vertices and a designated output vertex, such that
>
> • $G$ can be 3-colored *only* if its input vertices are colored with $T$'s and $F$'s.
>
> • For every sequence $b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n \in \{T, F\}$, there is a 3-coloring of $G$ in which the input vertices $v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_n \in V(G)$ have the colors $b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n \in \{T, F\}$.
>
> • In any 3-coloring of $G$ where the input vertices $v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_n \in V(G)$ have colors $b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n \in \{T, F\}$, the output vertex has color $f(b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n)$.
>
> For example, a 3-color-NOT-gate consists simply of two adjacent vertices. One vertex is designated to be the input vertex, $P$, and the other is designated to be the output vertex. Both vertices have to be constrained so they can only be colored with $T$'s or $F$'s in any proper 3-coloring. This constraint can be imposed by making them adjacent to the color-vertex $N$, as shown in Figure 11.28.
>
> (a) Verify that the graph in Figure 11.29 is a 3-color-OR-gate. (The dotted lines indicate edges to color-vertex $N$; these edges constrain the $P$, $Q$ and $P$ OR $Q$ vertices to be colored $T$ or $F$ in any proper 3-coloring.)
>
> (b) Let $E$ be an $n$-variable propositional formula, and suppose $E$ defines a truth function $f : \{T, F\}^n \to \{T, F\}$. Explain a simple way to construct a graph that is a 3-color-$f$-gate.
>
> (c) Explain why an efficient procedure for determining if a graph was 3-colorable would lead to an efficient procedure to solve the satisfiability problem, SAT.

〔习题原文，未译〕

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Figure 11.27（图 11.27）** Graph $G$ with no triangles and $\chi(G) = 4$ —— 一张没有 triangle（三角形）却需要四种颜色才能 proper coloring（正常着色）的 graph（图）：chromatic number（色数）$\chi(G)=4$，而每个 triangle-free（无三角形）的 graph（图）都只挡住「三色」这一条捷径，所以它是「三角形不足以解释色数」的最小反例形状。

> <span style="color:#1e8449;">**[译注]**</span>
> p453 的 3-color-$f$-gate（3-着色的 $f$-gate）是 6.042J 里少见的「把一种问题编码进另一种问题」的完整样本，读法应当逆着定义走：给定 truth function（真值函数）$f:\{T,F\}^n\to\{T,F\}$，要造一个 graph（图），使它的 proper 3-coloring（正常三点着色）与 $f$ 的输入输出表一一对应。机制全在那三个 color-vertex（颜色顶点）上：$T$、$F$、$N$ 两两 adjacent（相邻）构成 triangle（三角形），任何 proper 3-coloring（正常三点着色）里它们必然三色互异，于是「与 $N$ adjacent（相邻）」就成了一个 constraint（约束），把顶点逼成只能取 $T$ 或 $F$。连接路径：MIT 6.045/6.046（计算复杂度）里 3-coloring 是 NP-complete 的标准成员，归约链是 3SAT → NAE-3SAT → 3-coloring → planar 3-coloring，其中最后一步正是本块 Problem 11.40 用 cross-over gadget（交叉 gadget）做的（Stockmeyer 1973）；6.004（计算结构）里同一件事换个说法——VLSI 布线必须 planar（平面），所以「平面上的 gate（逻辑门）网络」才是可制造的电路，本节的 NOT / OR / XOR gate 就是那张电路图的 graph（图）版本。换句话说，本节习题在做的事，是造一台只用三种颜色就能读出 SAT 答案的机器。

<!-- ===== p454 ===== -->

本页只有两张图，都是 Figure 11.28 与 Figure 11.29 的 3-color gate（三点着色逻辑门）构造；题面文字在 p453 与 p455 两页。

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Figure 11.28（图 11.28）** A 3-color NOT-gate（一个 3-color NOT-gate / 三点着色取非门）—— 左侧两个相邻 vertex（顶点）分别标 $P$ 与 NOT($P$)，两者各经一条 dotted line（虚线，表示连到 $N$ 的 edge（边））接到 color-vertex（颜色顶点）$N$；$N$ 与 $T$、$F$ 构成 triangle（三角形），三者颜色必然互异，因此 $P$ 与 NOT($P$) 在任何 proper 3-coloring（正常三点着色）里只能取 $T$ 或 $F$，且必须取相反的那个。

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Figure 11.29（图 11.29）** A 3-color OR-gate（一个 3-color OR-gate / 三点着色或门）—— 左半仍是 $T$、$F$、$N$ 三个 color-vertex（颜色顶点）；右半是一个 6 个 node（节点）+ 2 个未标号 node（节点）的 gadget（小装置），$P$ 与 $Q$ 各经 dotted line（虚线）被约束到 $T/F$ 两色，顶端椭圆标 $P$ OR $Q$ 的 vertex（顶点）随之被迫取「或」的结果。虚线只表示「这条 edge（边）连到 $N$」，不参与 gadget（小装置）内部的计数。

<!-- ===== p455 ===== -->

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Figure 11.30（图 11.30）** A 3-color cross-over gadget（一个 3-color cross-over gadget / 三点着色交叉 gadget）—— 外围 face（面）是一个 cycle（圈），四个 designate（指定）vertex（顶点）$u,v,w,x$ 按顺时针排列；它的作用是把平面上 unavoidable（不可避免）的 edge crossing（边交叉）替换成一段 planar（平面）的小图，从此「任意 graph（图）的三着色」可以无损地搬到平面图上去做。两条性质（任一 $u,v$ 配色都能补全；任何三着色里 $u$ 与 $w$ 同色、$v$ 与 $x$ 同色）就是「交叉处信息不丢」的精确表述。

> **Problem 11.40.**
>
> The 3-coloring problem for planar graphs turns out to be no easier than the 3-coloring problem for arbitrary graphs. This claim follows very simply from the existence of a “3-color cross-over gadget.” Such a gadget is a planar graph whose outer face is a cycle with four designated vertices $u, v, w, x$ occurring in clockwise order such that
>
> 1. Any assignment of colors to vertices $u$ and $v$ can be completed into a 3-coloring of the gadget.
>
> 2. In every 3-coloring of the gadget, the colors of $u$ and $w$ are the same, and the colors of $v$ and $x$ are the also same.
>
> Figure 11.30 shows such a 3-color cross-over gadget.$^{12}$
>
> So to find a 3-coloring for any simple graph, simply draw it in the plane with edges crossing as needed, and then replace each occurrence of an edge crossing by a copy of the gadget as shown in Figure 11.31. This yields a planar graph which has a 3-coloring iff the original graph had one.
>
> (a) Prove that the graph in Figure 11.30 satisfies condition (1) by exhibiting the claimed 3-colorings.

〔习题原文，未译〕

> <span style="color:#1e8449;">**脚注 12（原文页脚）**</span>
> This gadget and reduction of 3-colorability to planar 3-colorability are due to Larry Stockmeyer [42].

<!-- ===== p456 ===== -->

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Figure 11.31（图 11.31）** Replacing an edge-crossing with a planar gadget（用平面 gadget（小装置）替换一条边交叉）—— 左图是两条 edge（边）在平面上的 crossing（交叉），右图把交叉点整体换成一个 planar（平面）小图：四个端点的接线位置不变，但内部不再有 crossing（交叉）。

> Hint: Only two colorings are needed, one where $u$ and $v$ are the same color and another where they are not the same color.
>
> (b) Prove that the graph in Figure 11.30 satisfies condition (2).
>
> Hint: The colorings for part (a) are almost completely forced by the coloring of $u$ and $v$.

〔习题原文，未译〕

### Exam Problems（考试题）

> **Problem 11.41.**
>
> False Claim. Let $G$ be a graph whose vertex degrees are all $\le k$. If $G$ has a vertex of degree strictly less than $k$, then $G$ is $k$-colorable.
>
> (a) Give a counterexample to the False Claim when $k = 2$.
>
> (b) Underline the exact sentence or part of a sentence that is the first unjustified step in the following bogus proof of the False Claim.
>
> Bogus proof. Proof by induction on the number $n$ of vertices:
>
> The induction hypothesis, $P(n)$ is:
>
> Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph whose vertex degrees are all $\le k$. If $G$ also has a vertex of degree strictly less than $k$, then $G$ is $k$-colorable.
>
> Base case: ($n = 1$) $G$ has one vertex, the degree of which is $0$. Since $G$ is 1-colorable, $P(1)$ holds.
>
> Inductive step: We may assume $P(n)$. To prove $P(n+1)$, let $G_{n+1}$ be a graph with $n+1$ vertices whose vertex degrees are all $k$ or less. Also, (continues on p457)

〔习题原文，未译〕

<!-- ===== p457 ===== -->

（承上页 Problem 11.41(b) 的 Bogus proof（伪证明）末句；以下整段是该伪证明的剩余部分，结尾的 $\square$ 是原书 QED 记号。）

> suppose $G_{n+1}$ has a vertex, $v$, of degree strictly less than $k$. Now we only need to prove that $G_{n+1}$ is $k$-colorable.
>
> To do this, first remove the vertex $v$ to produce a graph, $G_n$, with $n$ vertices. Let $u$ be a vertex that is adjacent to $v$ in $G_{n+1}$. Removing $v$ reduces the degree of $u$ by 1. So in $G_n$, vertex $u$ has degree strictly less than $k$. Since no edges were added, the vertex degrees of $G_n$ remain $\le k$. So $G_n$ satisfies the conditions of the induction hypothesis, $P(n)$, and so we conclude that $G_n$ is $k$-colorable.
>
> Now a $k$-coloring of $G_n$ gives a coloring of all the vertices of $G_{n+1}$, except for $v$. Since $v$ has degree less than $k$, there will be fewer than $k$ colors assigned to the nodes adjacent to $v$. So among the $k$ possible colors, there will be a color not used to color these adjacent nodes, and this color can be assigned to $v$ to form a $k$-coloring of $G_{n+1}$. $\square$
>
> (c) With a slightly strengthened condition, the preceding proof of the False Claim could be revised into a sound proof of the following Claim:
>
> Claim. Let $G$ be a graph whose vertex degrees are all $\le k$. If ⟨statement inserted from below⟩ has a vertex of degree strictly less than $k$, then $G$ is $k$-colorable.
>
> Circle each of the statements below that could be inserted to make the proof correct.
>
> • $G$ is connected and
>
> • $G$ has no vertex of degree zero and
>
> • $G$ does not contain a complete graph on $k$ vertices and
>
> • every connected component of $G$
>
> • some connected component of $G$

> **Problem 11.44.**
>
> The entire field of graph theory began when Euler asked whether the seven bridges of Königsberg could all be crossed exactly once. Abstractly, we can represent the parts of the city separated by rivers as vertices and the bridges as edges between the vertices. Then Euler's question asks whether there is a closed walk through the graph that includes every edge in a graph exactly once. In his honor, such a walk is called an Euler tour.
>
> So how do you tell in general whether a graph has an Euler tour? At first glance this may seem like a daunting problem. The similar sounding problem of finding a cycle that touches every vertex exactly once is one of those Millenium Prize NP-complete problems known as the Hamiltonian Cycle Problem. But it turns out to be easy to characterize which graphs have Euler tours.
>
> Theorem. A connected graph has an Euler tour if and only if every vertex has even degree.

〔习题原文，未译〕

<!-- ===== p459 ===== -->

> (a) Show that if a graph has an Euler tour, then the degree of each of its vertices is even.
>
> In the remaining parts, we'll work out the converse: if the degree of every vertex of a connected finite graph is even, then it has an Euler tour. To do this, let's define an Euler walk to be a walk that includes each edge at most once.
>
> (b) Suppose that an Euler walk in a connected graph does not include every edge. Explain why there must be an unincluded edge that is incident to a vertex on the walk.
>
> In the remaining parts, let $w$ be the longest Euler walk in some finite, connected graph.
>
> (c) Show that if $w$ is a closed walk, then it must be an Euler tour. Hint: part (b)
>
> (d) Explain why all the edges incident to the end of $w$ must already be in $w$.
>
> (e) Show that if the end of $w$ was not equal to the start of $w$, then the degree of the end would be odd. Hint: part (d)
>
> (f) Conclude that if every vertex of a finite, connected graph has even degree, then it has an Euler tour.

〔习题原文，未译〕

> <span style="color:#1e8449;">**[译注]**</span>
> Problem 11.44 的六个小问是一条完整的证明流水线，值得当定理来读：必要方向只用到 Handshaking Lemma（握手引理）——Euler tour（欧拉回路）经过每个 vertex（顶点）时必定一进一出、进出成对，故 degree（度）必为偶数；充分方向则用「取最长 Euler walk（欧拉走道）」的 extremal argument（极值论证），(d)(e) 两问其实在证明同一件事：若走道两端不重合，则两端 degree（度）为奇数，与假设冲突，于是它是 closed walk（闭走道），再由 (c) 升级成 tour（回路）。这条论证的工程形态就是 MIT 6.006 的 Hierholzer 算法：任取 vertex（顶点）沿未用 edge（边）走，遇死路就把当前 cycle（环）缝合进结果，总代价 $O(|E|)$。对照面极其刺眼——「每个 vertex（顶点）恰访问一次」的 Hamiltonian Cycle Problem（哈密顿回路问题）是 Millenium Prize 级的 NP-complete，而「每条 edge（边）恰走一次」线性时间可解。连接路径：本节 → 6.006 图搜索与 de Bruijn sequence（用于测序拼接、穷举所有 $n$-bit 串）→ 6.046 里「欧拉性只是每个顶点上的局部条件、哈密顿性却是全局条件」这一组对偶，它也是理解「P 与 NP 的边界为什么这么不整齐」的最小例子。

> **Problem 11.48.**
>
> False Claim. If every vertex in a graph has positive degree, then the graph is connected.
>
> (a) Prove that this Claim is indeed false by providing a counterexample.
>
> (b) Since the Claim is false, there must be a logical mistake in the following bogus proof. Pinpoint the first logical mistake (unjustified step) in the proof.
>
> Bogus proof. We prove the Claim above by induction. Let $P(n)$ be the proposition that if every vertex in an $n$-vertex graph has positive degree, then the graph is connected.
>
> Base cases: ($n \le 2$). In a graph with 1 vertex, that vertex cannot have positive degree, so $P(1)$ holds vacuously.
>
> $P(2)$ holds because there is only one graph with two vertices of positive degree, namely, the graph with an edge between the vertices, and this graph is connected.
>
> Inductive step: We must show that $P(n)$ implies $P(n+1)$ for all $n \ge 2$. Consider an $n$-vertex graph in which every vertex has positive degree. By the assumption $P(n)$, this graph is connected; that is, there is a path between every pair of vertices. Now we add one more vertex $x$ to obtain an $(n+1)$-vertex graph:

〔习题原文，未译〕

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Figure（图，原书此处未编号）** Problem 11.48(b) 伪证明的归纳步示意 —— 左侧单个 vertex（顶点）$x$ 经一条 edge（边）接到轮廓内的 $y$，轮廓内是一个 $n$-node connected graph（$n$ 个节点的连通图），$z$ 是其中任取的另一个 vertex（顶点）。漏洞在图的左边：$x$ 只与 $y$ 相连，而右侧那块图的连通性来自归纳假设 $P(n)$——可 $P(n)$ 的前提是「这块 $n$ 点图自身每个顶点 degree（度）为正」，一旦把它从整张图里摘出来，这个前提就不再被保证。

> All that remains is to check that there is a path from $x$ to every other vertex $z$. Since $x$ has positive degree, there is an edge from $x$ to some other vertex, $y$. Thus, we can obtain a path from $x$ to $z$ by going from $x$ to $y$ and then following the path from $y$ to $z$. This proves $P(n+1)$.

〔习题原文，未译〕

<!-- ===== p462 ===== -->

> By the principle of induction, $P(n)$ is true for all $n \ge 0$, which proves the Claim. $\square$

### Homework Problems（家庭作业题）

> **Problem 11.49.**
>
> An edge is said to *leave* a set of vertices if one end of the edge is in the set and the other end is not.
>
> (a) An $n$-node graph is said to be *mangled* if there is an edge leaving every set of $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ or fewer vertices. Prove the following:
>
> Claim. Every mangled graph is connected.
>
> An $n$-node graph is said to be *tangled* if there is an edge leaving every set of $\lceil n/3 \rceil$ or fewer vertices.
>
> (b) Draw a tangled graph that is not connected.
>
> (c) Find the error in the bogus proof of the following
>
> False Claim. Every tangled graph is connected.
>
> Bogus proof. The proof is by strong induction on the number of vertices in the graph. Let $P(n)$ be the proposition that if an $n$-node graph is tangled, then it is connected. In the base case, $P(1)$ is true because the graph consisting of a single node is trivially connected.
>
> For the inductive case, assume $n \ge 1$ and $P(1), \ldots, P(n)$ hold. We must prove $P(n+1)$, namely, that if an $(n+1)$-node graph is tangled, then it is connected. So let $G$ be a tangled, $(n+1)$-node graph. Choose $\lceil n/3 \rceil$ of the vertices and let $G_1$ be the tangled subgraph of $G$ with these vertices and $G_2$ be the tangled subgraph with the rest of the vertices. Note that since $n \ge 1$, the graph $G$ has a least two vertices, and so both $G_1$ and $G_2$ contain at least one vertex. Since $G_1$ and $G_2$ are tangled, we may assume by strong induction that both are connected. Also, since $G$ is tangled, there is an edge leaving the vertices of $G_1$ which necessarily connects to a vertex of $G_2$. This means there is a path between any two vertices of $G$: a path within one subgraph if both vertices are in the same subgraph, and a path traversing the connecting edge if the vertices are in separate subgraphs. Therefore, the entire graph, $G$, is connected. This completes the proof of the inductive case, and the Claim follows by strong induction. $\square$

> **Problem 11.67.**
>
> Let $G$ be a $4 \times 4$ grid with vertical and horizontal edges between neighboring vertices. Formally,
```math
V(G) = [0,3]^2 := \{(k,j) \mid 0 \le k,j \le 3\}.
```
> Letting $h_{i,j}$ be the horizontal edge $\langle (i,j)\text{—}(i+1,j)\rangle$ and $v_{j,i}$ be the vertical edge $\langle (j,i)\text{—}(j,i+1)\rangle$ for $i \in [0,2]$, $j \in [0,3]$, the weights of these edges are
```math
\begin{aligned}
w(h_{i,j}) &:= \frac{4i+j}{100},\\
w(v_{j,i}) &:= 1 + \frac{i+4j}{100}.
\end{aligned}
```
> (A picture of $G$ would help; you might like to draw one.)
>
> (a) Construct a minimum weight spanning tree (MST) for $G$ by initially selecting the minimum weight edge, and then successively selecting the minimum weight edge that does not create a cycle with the previously selected edges. Stop when the selected edges form a spanning tree of $G$. (This is Kruskal's MST algorithm.)
>
> (b) Grow an MST for $G$ starting with the tree consisting of the single vertex $(1,2)$ and successively adding the minimum weight edge with exactly one endpoint in the tree. Stop when the tree spans $G$. (This is Prim's MST algorithm.)
>
> (c) Grow an MST for $G$ by treating the vertices $(0,0), (0,3), (2,3)$ as 1-vertex trees and then successively adding, for each tree in parallel, the minimum weight (continues on p470)

〔习题原文，未译〕

> <span style="color:#1e8449;">**[译注]**</span>
> Problem 11.66–11.70 是 6.042J 把「贪心为什么对」讲得最干净的一处。11.66 要证的命题（唯一最小 weight（权重）的 edge（边）必在任一 MST（最小生成树）里）就是 cut property（割性质）的雏形：删掉这条 edge（边）把 vertex（顶点）分成两侧，任何跨过这条割的 edge（边）都比它重，于是用 exchange argument（交换论证）——若某 MST（最小生成树）不含它，把跨割的另一条 edge（边）换进来，weight（权重）严格下降，矛盾。11.67 三小问分别是 Kruskal、Prim 与 gray edge method（灰边法，即并行版本），要求对同一张 $4\times 4$ grid（网格）算三遍并核对结果一致；11.70 则用「取 $M\setminus N$ 中最小的那条 edge（边）」这同一套交换论证，证明 weight（权重）互不相同时 MST（最小生成树）唯一。连接路径：MIT 6.006 的 MST（最小生成树）讲义把这两点收成一组对偶定理（cut property 与 cycle property），6.046 再往上抽象成 matroid（拟阵）上的贪心正确性——「独立集系统满足交换公理 ⇒ 贪心最优」；18.06 那一侧则是 Laplacian（拉普拉斯矩阵）$L=D-A$ 的 spectrum（谱）给出「割」的代数刻画（Cheeger 不等式），也就是谱聚类与图分割的起点。对做题的人只须记一句：MST（最小生成树）的所有证明都是「换一条 edge（边）、看 weight（权重）怎么变」。

<!-- ===== p470 ===== -->

> edge among the edges with one endpoint in the tree. Continue as long as there is no edge between two trees, then go back to applying the general gray edge method until the parallel trees merge to form a spanning tree of $G$. (This is 6.042's parallel MST algorithm.)

> (d) Verify that you got the same MST each time.
